Good questions — TL;DR first, then a worked example.

1) Tokens vs characters vs requests
- Tokens are the billing unit. A token is roughly ~4 English characters on average (so 1,000 tokens ~= 4,000 chars), but the exact conversion depends on language and punctuation.
- Requests are API calls (one request can contain many tokens: input + output). We charge based on billed tokens (input tokens + output tokens), not per request.

2) Prompt caching and billed tokens
- Caching is prefix-based: when you have identical prefix text across requests (e.g., shared system prompt, instructions, or long static context), Redwood can cache the KV cache and avoid re-sending/rehashing that work on the GPU.
- Billing effect: when a cache hit occurs, you are generally not billed for the cached input tokens again for that request (we only bill for the non-cached tokens and the generated output tokens). There are corner cases (partial hits) where billed tokens are prorated; we can share exact rules in the pricing-sheet appendix.

3) Worked example for your pilot (10k req/day) — using assumptions you suggested: avg request = 300 tokens (input + output combined).
- 300 tokens/request * 10,000 requests/day = 3,000,000 tokens/day -> 90,000,000 tokens/month (30-day month).
- If your target cost is $X per 1M tokens, monthly cost = (tokens_month / 1,000,000) * $X.

Example unit economics (two scenarios we typically quote):
A) Hosted standard model: $25 per 1M tokens -> 90M tokens/month = 90 * $25 = $2,250/month (pilot)
B) Higher-capacity model / smaller-latency path: $120 per 1M tokens -> 90M * $120 = $10,800/month

Note: these are illustrative prices — final quote will depend on model family, output lengths, and any reserved capacity discounts. If you can reduce average tokens/request (e.g., via prompt engineering or more caching on shared prefixes), cost drops linearly. For example, with 50% effective prefix caching of a 100-token header, billed tokens could reduce by ~500K tokens/day in your pilot example (material savings).

4) Converting chars -> tokens for your prompts
- If prompts are 1,500–3,000 chars, that’s roughly 375–750 tokens (using ~4 chars/token). Add model output tokens on top of that. If you expect outputs of ~150 tokens, then total per request might be 525–900 tokens. 

I attached a simple calc in example-usage.csv and updated the pricing-sheet.pdf appendix. I can also run your real prompt examples through our tokenizer and give exact tokens and a line-item cost per 30-day run.

Next steps: if $25/1M tokens (scenario A) looks attractive, that maps to well under your $20k/month pilot budget in the example above. If you prefer a conservative quote for higher-capacity model we can show $120/1M and walk through reserved vs usage pricing.

Let me know which model class you'd like us to run numbers for and I’ll produce a formal quote (DocuSign link).
